fixes.explanation: King Herod shows up earlier in Matthew's Gospel (Matthew 2:1), but not here. The text says the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness "…to be tempted by the devil." (Matthew 4:1) So this isn't a hiding trip. Jesus goes out there led by the Spirit.

Bread it is. The tempter says, "If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread." (Matthew 4:3) Jesus had fasted forty days and forty nights, so I think a loaf looked pretty good right about then. Friend, I'd have been tempted too.

Fire from heaven is a big dramatic moment in other Bible stories, like 1 Kings 18:38, but not in this one. On the pinnacle of the temple, the devil says, "throw Yourself down." (Matthew 4:6) That's the dare. It's about jumping, not about fire.

That's right. Jesus replies, "It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’…" (Matthew 4:7) The devil said "it is written" first, and Jesus answers with Scripture too. Jesus points to another line instead of taking the jump.

The prophets don't come up in this scene. Jesus says, "Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only." (Matthew 4:10) The worship goes to the Lord your God. That word "only" leaves no room for anyone else.

That's it. The text says, "Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him." (Matthew 4:11) Right after Jesus says, "Away from Me, Satan!" the devil leaves. Then angels come and minister to Jesus. The three tests are done.
